newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Pact to scrap tariffs in infotech trade clinched.
newsitem.headline: Pact to scrap tariffs in infotech trade clinched.

text.p: A total of 39 countries on Wednesday agreed on a $500 billion global pact to scrap tariffs in the booming information technology trade by the year 2000, WTO chief Renato Ruggiero told reporters.
The landmark information technology pact will benefit customers, manufacturers and global trade, according to industry analysts and officials at the 130-member trade watchdog.
Poland and Panama, who had been expected to take part in the tariff-scrapping agreement, were not among the 39 countries for "operational reasons", according to WTO officials.
The accord, under which the first tariff cuts must take place in July, was shaped in December by ministers meeting in Singapore under WTO auspices.

Tariffs are to be cut in four stages between 1997 and 2000 in five main product categories: computers, telecom products, semiconductors, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, software including diskettes and CD ROMs and scientific instruments.
